Name: Santo Domingo Church & Museum
Brief Description: 16th-century baroque monastery with gold-leafed interiors and Museum of Oaxacan Cultures displaying Monte Albán treasures

Name: Mercado Benito Juárez
Brief Description: Oaxaca's central market featuring mole, chocolate, mezcal, tlayudas, chapulines, handicrafts, and local food stalls

Name: Monte Albán Archaeological Site
Brief Description: Major Zapotec capital (500 BCE-800 CE) atop artificially flattened mountain with Great Plaza, ball court, and panoramic views

Name: El Árbol del Tule
Brief Description: 2,000-year-old Montezuma cypress with world's widest tree trunk (58m circumference) and 42m height

Name: Mitla Archaeological Zone
Brief Description: Post-Classic Zapotec site (900-1521 CE) famous for intricate geometric stone mosaics and palace structures

Name: Tehuantepec City Center
Brief Description: Colonial city and cornerstone of Isthmus Zapotec culture with Templo de Santo Domingo and traditional market

Name: Guiengola Archaeological Site
Brief Description: Ancient Zapotec mountain fortress above Tehuantepec, last stronghold against Aztec conquest with spectacular views

Name: Temple San Vicente Ferrer
Brief Description: 17th-century church in Juchitán, oldest in the city, dedicated to patron saint with battle monument

Name: Juchitán Central Market
Brief Description: Massive traditional market dominated by women merchants, famous for textiles, handicrafts, and traditional foods

Name: Puerto Madero
Brief Description: Chiapas's main Pacific port and commercial fishing center with fresh seafood restaurants and nearby beaches

Name: Parque Miguel Hidalgo Tapachula
Brief Description: Beautiful central plaza with Indian laurel trees, colonial lampposts, marimba performances, surrounding Cathedral and Municipal Palace

Name: Museo Arqueológico Soconusco
Brief Description: Archaeological museum in Tapachula featuring artifacts from Soconusco region including Izapa culture pieces

Name: Izapa Archaeological Zone
Brief Description: Massive pre-Columbian site (1500 BCE-1200 CE) bridging Olmec and Maya cultures with 89 stelae, 61 altars oriented toward Tacaná

Name: Volcán Tacaná
Brief Description: Second highest peak in Central America (4,060m), active stratovolcano on Mexico-Guatemala border in protected biosphere reserve

Name: Unión Juárez
Brief Description: Picturesque mountain village with Swiss-style houses, cool climate, coffee plantations, gateway to Tacaná Volcano climbing

Name: Playa Linda
Brief Description: Pacific beach near Tapachula with strong waves, expansive sand, ideal for water sports and swimming

Name: Playa Costa Azul Pijijiapan
Brief Description: Beach after estuary crossing with calm lagoon waters and ocean waves, ideal for boat tours and water sports

Name: La Encrucijada Reserve
Brief Description: Biosphere reserve with world's tallest mangroves (35m), estuaries, sea turtles, and rich biodiversity

Name: Finca Hamburgo
Brief Description: Historic early 20th-century coffee plantation in California-style with art nouveau decoration, museum and restaurant

Name: Finca Rosario Izapa
Brief Description: Research center near Izapa for cacao and tropical fruits, offers tours of traditional cultivation methods
